You are the Diagram Topology Agent. Extract explicit semantic topology from ORIGINAL methodology/caption, not from reference-image contents or an embellished plan. Return ONLY JSON:
{"schemaVersion":1,"nodes":[{"id":"stable_id","label":"exact supplied name","shape":"process|decision|terminal|initial","role":"normal|initial|terminal"}],"edges":[{"id":"edge_id","source":"node_id","target":"node_id","label":"event or condition, or empty string","sourceQuote":"verbatim supporting substring from original methodology/caption"}],"uncertainties":[],"layout":{"direction":"RIGHT|DOWN"}}.
Every source, target, direction and event/condition must be supported by original text. Every required relation must be represented, including returns, reverse/parallel edges and self loops. Source quotes are provenance, NOT proof of correct inference. Preserve all stated labels. A shared end/state is one node ID even with multiple incoming edges; do not merge unrelated nodes. Initial dot is a distinct shape initial node with empty label and role initial. Named start is shape terminal with role initial. Only truly terminal nodes have role terminal; any reset/outgoing transition excludes terminal role. Decision shape is diamond, operations process. Do not add inferred relations to make a connected drawing. If missing/ambiguous, populate uncertainties; the pipeline will stop without inventing relationships. Bounds 2–24 nodes, 1–48 edges, node label <=100 characters, edge label <=80. Layout never changes semantics. Reference images influence visual style only. Actual output viewport is supplied in context.

  "originalRequest": "Synthetic teaching example of an instrument state machine. States: Idle, Running, Paused, Completed. Initial dot enters Idle. Transitions: Idle→Running: start; Running→Paused: pause; Paused→Running: resume; Running→Completed: finish; Paused→Idle: cancel; Completed→Idle: reset. Each named state appears once. Arrows are labelled events, not process activities. Completed is not a terminal state because reset returns to Idle. English text. Reference is for structural design only.",

  "completePlan": "Based on the methodology and the visual style of the reference image (specifically Panel B), here is a detailed description for the illustrative figure.\n\n**Figure Description:**\n\n**Overall Layout & Style:**\nThe image is a schematic state transition diagram presented on a pure white background. The style is minimalist and high-contrast, utilizing black lines and text with no color fills other than white. The layout follows a logical flow from left to right, representing the lifecycle of an instrument, but includes a feedback loop to demonstrate the non-terminal nature of the \"Completed\" state.\n\n**Nodes (States):**\nThere are four distinct state nodes, represented as rectangles with rounded corners (pill-shaped or similar to the reference). Each node has a thick black outline (approx. 2pt) and a white interior. Inside each node, the state name is centered in a bold, sans-serif font (e.g., Arial or Helvetica), sized roughly 14-16pt.\n1.  **Idle:** Located on the far left, vertically centered. This is the starting point.\n2.  **Running:** Located to the right of \"Idle\", slightly higher than the vertical center.\n3.  **Paused:** Located directly below \"Running\", creating a vertical column for the active states.\n4.  **Completed:** Located to the right of \"Running\", aligned horizontally with it.\n\n**Initial State Indicator:**\nA solid black circle (dot), approximately 1/3 the height of the state nodes, is positioned to the immediate left of the \"Idle\" node. A short, straight horizontal arrow connects this dot to the left edge of the \"Idle\" node, indicating the entry point into the system.\n\n**Transitions (Edges & Labels):**\nConnections between states are depicted as solid black lines with filled triangular arrowheads indicating direction. Each transition line is labeled with the triggering event in a smaller, regular-weight sans-serif font (approx. 10-12pt), placed near the midpoint of the line.\n\n*   **Idle $\\rightarrow$ Running:** A straight horizontal arrow pointing right from \"Idle\" to \"Running\". Label: **\"start\"** (placed above the arrow).\n*   **Running $\\rightarrow$ Paused:** A straight vertical arrow pointing down from \"Running\" to \"Paused\". Label: **\"pause\"** (placed to the right of the arrow).\n*   **Paused $\\rightarrow$ Running:** A straight vertical arrow pointing up from \"Paused\" to \"Running\", running parallel to the \"pause\" arrow. Label: **\"resume\"** (placed to the left of the arrow).\n*   **Running $\\rightarrow$ Completed:** A straight horizontal arrow pointing right from \"Running\" to \"Completed\". Label: **\"finish\"** (placed above the arrow).\n*   **Paused $\\rightarrow$ Idle:** A long, curved arrow originating from the left side of the \"Paused\" node. It sweeps downwards and then curves upwards and leftwards to point into the bottom of the \"Idle\" node. Label: **\"cancel\"** (placed below the curve).\n*   **Completed $\\rightarrow$ Idle:** A long, curved arrow originating from the top or right side of the \"Completed\" node. It arcs significantly over the top of the \"Running\" node (to avoid overlap) and points down into the top of the \"Idle\" node. This visualizes the reset mechanism. Label: **\"reset\"** (placed above the highest point of the arc).\n\n**Visual Consistency Notes:**\n*   Ensure all arrowheads are uniform in size and shape.\n*   Ensure the curvature of the \"cancel\" and \"reset\" arrows is smooth and distinct, clearly separating them from the central linear flow.\n*   Text alignment should be precise; labels should not touch the arrow lines.\n*   The diagram contains no title or caption text within the image boundaries.",

The Boolean functions are represented by the edges. (B) State transition diagram of all 2^{3} = 8 states of the BN represented in (A). (C) Simplification of a bBM for a phosphorylation-dephosphorylation system as elemental species-reaction graph. The nodes corresponding to elemental states of component x_{1} are shown in black, the nodes corresponding to reactions are shown with grey fillings. Here, a component (protein) x_{1} undergoes phosphorylation by consuming its elemental state x_{1}-{0} to produce its modified state x_{1}-{P} by reaction r_{1} (phosphorylation). The modified x_{1}-{P} undergoes consumption thereby producing the neutral state x_{1}-{0} via reaction r_{2} (dephosphorylation) (details in [29]). When at least either of the two elemental states x_{1}-{0} or x_{1}-{P} are active in the initial state, both will be active in the attractor.
